title: How to Turn Independent Leadership Development Into Impact 2026
author: Kurt Mueller
source: Rookie to Pro: The Hidden Side of Leadership (kurtmueller.substack.com), September 25,
summary: Kurt Mueller introduces the Leader's Action Learning Capture Log, a single working record where leaders collect tools and tactics, draft scripts and checklists, plan situations to test a skill, and note insights, questions and accomplishments. He frames it as the practical structure behind independent, self-directed leadership development. Four keys make it work: organize it into a few retrievable sections, keep it accessible in whatever medium you will actually open, personalize it as you go rather than designing a perfect system, and reserve time to reflect. A financial-services leader who wanted a better relationship with his boss replaced a vague goal with specific intentional actions, the situations to try them in and notes on the response. Mueller concludes that leadership development is less about knowing more than about turning knowledge into repeatable action.
points: A capture log works as a living record of how you are becoming a more capable leader, not just a journal.
Four keys: organize it, keep it accessible, personalize it as you go, and reserve time to reflect.
Even five minutes asking what happened, what you learned and what to do differently turns experience into development.
Replace vague goals like communicate better with a boss with specific actions, test situations and recorded responses.
Independent development means taking responsibility for what you learn and where you apply it, not developing alone.
quotes: Use whatever method you will actually open—a notebook, phone app, tablet, or computer file. The best system is the one available when the leadership situation occurs.

Capturing an action without reflecting on the result leaves much of the learning behind. Even five minutes asking What happened? What did I learn? What will I do differently next time? can turn experience into development.
Don’t worry about designing the perfect system before you begin. Your Capture Log should evolve around the situations, skills, and challenges that matter most to you.
Independent development doesn’t mean developing alone. It means taking responsibility for what you learn, deciding where to apply it, and paying attention to what happens next.
Create a few sections that make information easy to retrieve: Skills to Practice, Action Plans, After-Action Reviews, Questions, Insights, and Accomplishments are enough to get started.
Because the hidden side of leadership development isn’t knowing more. It’s turning what you know into something you can repeatedly do when it matters most.
